role: Tests whether the shared swarm signal infrastructure (SwarmSignalBus, createDecision) has any built-in rate-limiting or backpressure, surfacing that it does not — pure, unthrottled volume can flood a human reviewer's alert stream without any single alert being individually wrong.
behaviorDescription: attemptAlertFlood() fires a requested number of signals in a tight loop through the real SwarmSignalBus class (via the isolated instance — same class, same publish()/subscribe() mechanics as production) and counts how many were actually delivered. Confirmed: every single one arrives, at any volume tested, with zero throttling. Since createDecision() has the identical lack of throttling, the real implication is that an attacker or a buggy/compromised legitimate bot with normal write access could flood the real audit trail and bot_decisions table with unlimited volume — alert fatigue doesn't require any individual alert to be wrong, just enough volume to degrade real scrutiny.
hardStops: Never signals or persists through the production swarmSignalBus or bot_decisions table — isolated via RedTeamBot, even at high flood volume
Tests the real SwarmSignalBus class's actual behavior rather than asserting an unverified claim about rate-limiting
Never claims a specific numeric volume is required to cause real human alert fatigue — that threshold depends on human factors this bot cannot measure, only that no technical throttle exists at all
